description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 2 on t/op/eval.t:185).

perl: the lexical search an `eval STRING` performs stops at the boundary of
the sub it is written in.  A free name that is not a lexical of THAT sub is
the package variable, never the caller's lexical.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    $main::r = "good";
    sub terminal { eval '$r . q{!}' }
    print do { my $r = "bad"; eval 'terminal($r)' }, "\n";

    perl: good!      ($r inside `terminal` is $main::r)
    PCL:  !          ($r is undef -- neither the caller's lexical nor the global)

So PCL gets the SCOPING right (it does not leak the caller's `my $r`) and the
FALLBACK wrong: the free name resolves to nothing instead of to the package
variable.  The run-time free-name resolution in `p-eval-thunk` is the place
that already answers "unqualified -> current package" (the #240 step-2 work),
so the miss is that the capture alist's absence is not falling through to it
on this path.

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/eval.t 40 `lexical search terminates
correctly at subroutine boundary`.


=== NOTE (s535a, 2026-11-08) -- the one row keyed on this task PASSES; CLOSE-WITH-ROWS candidate ===
t/op/eval.t row 40 ("lexical search terminates correctly at subroutine boundary") passes on the s535a tree (companion one-file, scratch/s535a/comp2.log: base 06a4b8ba 137/31 = the snapshot, tree 138/30) and left baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv by edit -- it was the last row carrying #1957.  The reproducer above already prints `good!` on the base 06a4b8ba (probe scratch/s535a/pr/q14.pl in the s535a worktree: perl = base = tree); what kept the FILE's row failing was the legacy span pass over-promoting t/op/eval.t's later block `$r` to a file cell `$r__file__N`, which terminal()'s eval alist carried.  Port 3 (the span pass on Pl::Binder::spans) makes no such cell.  The related shape with a GENUINELY spanning later lexical is #1455's (note there).  Status left as it is (the reviewing session closes).
subject: a STRING EVAL inside a sub whose free name matches no lexical does not fall back to the PACKAGE variable -- perl's lexical search stops at the sub boundary
